Truculent

/TRUK-yuh-luhnt/ - the stress falls on TRUK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Truculent means aggressively defiant; eager to fight.

The film's mechanic is truculent from her first line, answering a customer's 'good morning' with 'want to make something of it?'

Worked Example

Even in the retirement home's chess club, Mr. Baxter stays truculent, offering to settle stalemates 'the old way' until the nurses wheel him in to lunch.

Truculent is more than grouchy: it is aggression looking for an outlet, defiance that hopes you will push back. A surly person wants to be left alone; a truculent one is disappointed when the argument ends peacefully.

How Truculent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

belligerent

belligerent: ready for battle; hostility on a war footing

feisty

feisty: scrappy and spirited; often said with admiration

Antonyms

meek

meek: quietly submissive; slow to defend even oneself

peaceable

peaceable: disposed to avoid quarrels altogether

How Strong Is It? — prickly → quarrelsome → truculent

prickly vs. truculent

prickly vs. truculent: Prickly people bristle when handled wrong, but that is far from truculent's open hunt for a fight.

quarrelsome vs. truculent

quarrelsome vs. truculent: Quarrelsome picks verbal fights over anything; it stops short of truculent, which is ready to make the fight physical.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of truculent.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — truc

Root — truc: savage, fierce (Latin trux)

Suffix — -ulent

Suffix — -ulent: full of (as in turbulent, fraudulent)

Put it together

Put it together: Truc (savage — Latin trux) + -ulent (full of) = full of savagery. You know the ending from turbulent and fraudulent; the root trux left no other English descendants, so truculent stands alone — full of a fight that nothing else in the language picked.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Latin trux, 'savage,' entered English exactly once, inside truculent. Despite the sound, it is no relation to truce — an Old English word for a pledge of peace, nearly its opposite — or to truck. The -ulent ending, though, is the same 'full of' you see in turbulent and fraudulent.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / vivid

Truculent is for open, eager-to-fight defiance — a posture you can see across a room. Surly is unfriendly but passive; quarrelsome argues; truculent squares up. Malevolent (this unit) is darker: it wishes harm quietly, while truculent announces itself.
